ads.label: V1 · Two to three times cheaper
ads.flow: "If you just got quoted twenty thousand dollars or more" over the installer drilling a new frame (120 fps slow-mo) → quote/calculator → South Florida aerial → outside crew → "You end up paying extra twice" → VistaGuard pill over the crew installing → "Same hurricane rating" over storm palms → 30 years, licensed, lifetime warranty over finished jobs → CLICK "GET QUOTE" BELOW with arrow.
confirm: "Two to three times" cheaper and "over thirty years" are current claims.
Lifetime warranty covers products and materials as stated.

ads.label: V6 · Check the bottom of that quote
ads.flow: "Look at the bottom of it" over the drill shot and paperwork → labor line "can add thousands" → "installation is free" (whip to the crew) → own crew installs every window → direct from the manufacturer → 30 years / lifetime warranty over finished homes → caps CTA with arrow.
confirm: Free installation is still the offer.
"Two to three times less" claim.

ads.label: V3 · Why pay more? (all-out)
ads.script: Veer, Sept 2026 doc, Script 3 (mirrors the aired V2 winner: 1,001 leads at $30.51)
ads.flow: Opens on the installer's drill in 120 fps slow-mo under "Why pay twenty thousand dollars" → calculator → laser level → storm palms on "two to three times less" → VistaGuard pill over the crew → South Florida aerial → hurricane coast → whip into the install: direct from the manufacturer, own crew, no broker → flash cut on "installation is included, free" → prep, clean work, storms → 30 years / lifetime warranty over finished homes → caps CTA, ending on the same drill shot it opened on so the loop restarts cleanly. 36 cuts (1.4 s each), 7 zoom-blur whips, an impact zoom on every hard cut.
confirm: "Thousands of South Florida homeowners" and "over thirty years" claims.
Installation included free is still the offer.

ads.label: A1 · $1,995 direct, fair price
ads.flow: Gold "$1,995" lands over a quartzite waterfall island → dated granite (thousands more) → "fair price" → "sleep at night" → GC Countertops name pill (their logo file says "Granite Club", so it is not shown) → amazing work over GC's best islands → old tops out, core drill + marking, new white quartz on the same island → "100% happy" → glass Get Quote card.
confirm: $1,995 is a starting price (VO says "starting at").
"Contractor pricing" / 100% satisfaction wording approved.

ads.label: B1 · $30 per square foot + price table
ads.flow: Gold "$30" per square foot over two waterfall islands → Georgia homeowners → "no inflated quotes" → tape measure, clear price per sq ft → required on-screen table lands row by row as the VO says Granite from $30 · Quartz from $55 · Marble from $65 → start to finish, old tops out, new in → 10 years licensed and insured → glass "tap / Get Quote / below".
confirm: Table prices: Granite from $30, Quartz from $55, Marble from $65 per sq ft.
The supplied logo reads "Granite Club LLC · ESTD 2023", so it is NOT used (rule: never show Granite Club). The VO's "over 10 years" should refer to crew experience; confirm.

ads.label: B2 · Shocked by your quote? (all-out)
ads.flow: "If you got a quote… shocked… watch this" over a dark quartzite waterfall, the calculator and a dated granite kitchen, whipping to an onyx island → markup / paying more → GC Countertops pill with a whip → "contractor pricing" over the crew measuring, marking and core-drilling (no supplier or slab yard shown) → the required price table lands row by row as the VO says Granite $30 · Quartz $55 · Marble $65 → 100% satisfaction guarantee over finished kitchens → glass Get Quote, ending on the opening island. 30 cuts (1.5 s), 4 whips, impact zooms.
confirm: Table prices: Granite from $30, Quartz from $55, Marble from $65 per sq ft.
100% satisfaction guarantee wording approved.

ads.label: P1 · Seven-day showcase
ads.flow: "A bathroom remodel done in seven days" over a time-lapse remodel → Luxury Home Renovations pill → 10 outdated bathrooms, discounted, before/after videos → qualify: 5+ years old, full remodel or tub-to-shower, ready in 30 days → finished bathrooms → glass "hit / Get Quote / below".
confirm: Showcase offer (10 homes, discounted rate) is live.
No client footage yet: swap in their real bathrooms when shared.

ads.label: F1 · $14,995 full bathroom, what's included
ads.flow: Gold "$14,995" over a finished bathroom → "has to cost thirty thousand. It does not." → torn down and built back new → what you get: demo, waterproofing, tile or acrylic surrounds, glass door, vanity, toilet, flooring, fixtures → honest number before we start → LHR pill, 38 years licensed (captions blank over the state names, per the client rule) → own crews → showroom → 2-year labor warranty → glass Get Quote.
confirm: 38 years / two-year labor warranty claims.
No client footage yet: swap in their real bathrooms when shared.

ads.label: F2 · Biggest special ever, $14,995 (all-out)
ads.flow: "The biggest bathroom remodeling special we have ever run" over a hero bathroom, then the gold $14,995 pinned in the hook stack → whip into a full time-lapse remodel → every item gets its own cut, on the word: demo, shower/tub, waterproofing, tile or acrylic, glass door, vanity, toilet, flooring, fixtures → one team vs plumber/tile guy/electrician → showroom and samples → plans and itemized estimate → 2-year labor warranty → LHR pill, 38 years (captions blank over the state names) → glass Get Quote, ending on the opening bathroom. 57 cuts (1.4 s), 7 whips.
confirm: Biggest-special claim and $14,995 starting price.
No client footage yet: AI + stock bathrooms. Swap in their real bathrooms when shared.

ads.label: V5 · $19,995 that's crazy
ads.script: Aired Rob-Art V5 (4.07.26), word for word
ads.flow: Gold "$19,995" over Rob-Art's black-marble waterfall island → "like $40,000 usually" → size/layout/materials → "sleep at night" over a dated kitchen → Rob-Art Design LLC pill → amazing work, in-house NJ crews → big bloated companies → custom design, drawings, material selection → fair prices → glass Get Quote.
confirm: $19,995 premium kitchen offer still stands.

ads.label: V1 · Why pay $40,000
ads.script: Aired Rob-Art V1 (4.07.26), word for word
ads.flow: "Why pay $40,000" over their finished island → Rob-Art Design LLC pill, NJ since 2012 → consultation → real design drawings, then ONLY Rob-Art's real kitchens under "not AI pictures, not stock images" → material selection → in-house crew over their real befores (gutted oak kitchen) → "under $20,000" → glass Get Quote. No AI imagery in this ad.
confirm: Since 2012 and the under-$20,000 claim.

ads.label: V4 · $349 a month (all-out)
ads.script: Aired Rob-Art V4 (4.07.26), word for word: the account's workhorse ($20,310 spend, 235 leads)
ads.flow: Gold "$349 a month" over Rob-Art's black-marble island → a cut on each of "car payment" (hands on a wheel), "gym membership" (dumbbell rack) and "takeout coffee" (cup in a car holder) → their dated cherry kitchens on "can't afford it" → whip to the finished kitchen on "here's the reality", flash on "you can afford it" → calculator / $19,995 vs $349 → Rob-Art Design LLC pill, financing, custom kitchens → design options, swatches and plans → since 2012 / 12-month workmanship warranty over their real befores and afters → glass Get Quote, ending on the opening island. 39 cuts (1.4 s), 6 whips.
confirm: $349/month and $19,995 figures, and that financing is live (it is not on the banned list for Rob-Art).
12-month workmanship warranty and since-2012 claims.

update.title: Updated Oct 7: new voice, upbeat music, and a third all-out ad per client
items: Voice on all 12: ElevenLabs Michael re-read on the newer v4 model, which is crisper and brighter. It reads at house pace (185–212 wpm); 10 of 12 need no time-stretch and two get a light 4–5%. Finished with de-essing, presence and light compression.
Music on all 12: upbeat beds lifted from our own winning ads, 115–135 BPM instead of the old 88 BPM bed, sitting a dB or two louder under the voice.

A third ad for each client, cut for retention: about 1.4 s per shot (vs 1.9 s), 4–7 zoom-blur whips, an impact zoom on every hard cut, a cut on every listed item, and an ending that loops back to the opening frame.
The first eight ads keep their edit. Only the voice and music changed.
